decision.what_is_decided: At each step, which listed browser action best advances a free-form task, whether the goal already holds on this page/history, and whether the run is stuck. If a select action is chosen, which dropdown option to pick.

inputs.name: task
inputs.source: NavigateOptions from CLI or MCP caller
inputs.role: Natural-language goal every judgment is relative to

inputs.name: current_page
inputs.source: Playwright url and title after settle

inputs.name: page_text_excerpt
inputs.role: Readable page content to match against the task

inputs.name: interactive_elements
inputs.role: Candidate click/type/select targets for the action choice

inputs.name: history
inputs.source: Prior executed actions and observed outcomes this run
inputs.role: Progress, repeats, and loop evidence for stuck and next action

inputs.name: dropdown_options
inputs.role: Competing labels for the nested option choice

outcomes: one action id (click/type/select on an element, scroll_up/down, back, or done)
one dropdown option when a select_* action runs
decision.downstream_action: Before acting: stop if action is done, goal_done noul above 0.85, or stuck noul above 0.85 after step 2. Else run Playwright click/fill/scroll/back. Repeat-no-op may switch via pickAlternate. select_* asks Jev again then selectOption.

jev_questions.what_it_asks: Which single listed action best advances the task on the current page
Whether the current page and history already show the sought task outcome
Whether actions so far are not progressing (repeats, loops, or no change)
Which listed dropdown option to select given the task and page

semantic_ambiguity.evidence: Free-form task must be matched to short element descriptions and a truncated page excerpt; many controls can look equally relevant.

context_dependence.evidence: State bundle is task plus this page, excerpt, live element list, truncation flags, and step history; the same task needs different actions on different pages.

deterministic_expressibility.evidence: No closed mapping from arbitrary tasks and live DOMs to one control; success and stuck are readings of page plus history, not predicates on url or counts.

judgment_required.evidence: Questions ask which action advances the task and whether goal/stuck hold; code only thresholds those scores and executes the chosen id.

rule_stability.evidence: Correct action and done/stuck meaning change with every task, site, and page snapshot; a fixed rule table would not transfer.

risk_or_policy_component.evidence: Jev questions are progress and goal, not safety or policy. allowTyping is a caller flag enforced in code, not asked of Jev.

natural_language_understanding.evidence: Task string, page excerpt, element descriptions, and dropdown labels are language that must be interpreted together.

decision_complexity.evidence: One discrete choice over a generated action list plus two stop beliefs, and sometimes a nested option choice; hard semantically, not a large coupled rule net.

why_jev_hypotheses.evidence: askJev at navigate.ts:415 gets task, excerpt, and element descriptions and must pick which control advances that task; that is interpreting page meaning, not computing a formula.
Task is an unconstrained string (NavigateOptions). Page evidence is a short excerpt and 80-char labels (extractAndStamp/pageObservables). Labels and copy are inherently ambiguous.
action is a choice among many element actions plus scroll/back/done. Probabilities feed pickAlternate (navigate.ts:450-457) when two actions compete after a no-op.
Opening comment and structure: code extracts state and executes ids; Jev answers action/goal_done/stuck. Outcome-after-action (navigate.ts:522-532) is exact; the next-act decision is not.
No policy text or allowed/denied rules are passed into askJev. Questions are task advancement, goal achieved, and stuck, not compliance.
stuck is lack of progress, not harm. Stop gates (navigate.ts:431-445) halt the agent; they do not score safety risk.
Classifying the page as done/stuck/continue and picking an action id requires task plus this page plus history, assembled in state at navigate.ts:406-414.
Action space is rebuilt from whatever the live DOM offers each step. An exact rule would need per-site selectors and per-task success checks for unbounded pages.
goal_done and stuck are graded nouls with a later 0.85 cutoff, not boolean page predicates. What counts as the sought outcome is the current task wording, not a stable spec.
Excerpt is capped; element list can be truncated or empty; settle may give up (navigate.ts:277-296). History outcomes are coarse (navigated/content changed/no visible change).
Loop rebuilds state from the current page every step. Identical task on a new url/title/excerpt/history yields a new action choice.
Hand-written selectors or if-url-then-click recipes would break across sites. The code instead stamps live controls and asks Jev rather than encoding site scripts.

not_reasons.note: Stop-before-act matters to the run, but Jev is here because the page-vs-task call is semantic. Criticality alone would not pick Jev over a rule.
Usage/cost is tracked as a consequence of Jev (askJev budget). Expense is not a reason to use Jev; typing even falls back to a cheap heuristic.
navigate is long because of browser launch, settle, execution, and extraction. Jev is two ask sites; length does not explain those asks.
Branches after the choice (back/scroll/type/select/click) are deterministic Playwright. They consume the decision; they are not why it is judged.
This loop is the product core, but importance does not make a decision semantic. Jev fits the page/task judgment, not because the feature is central.
Hardening, timeouts, and observers are complex plumbing. The Jev questions themselves are small judgments over assembled state.

observed.claim: Each step sends task, page, excerpt, interactive elements, and history to Jev and reads action, goal_done, and stuck.

evidence.observation: State object is built then askJev is called with stepQuestions; answers.action.choice and the two noul scores are stored on the step.

observed.claim: Jev stop beliefs are applied before any browser action runs.

evidence.observation: If proposed is done, or goal_done noul exceeds 0.85, or stuck noul exceeds 0.85 after step 2, the loop records a null executed action and breaks.

observed.claim: Choosing a select action triggers a second Jev choice over dropdown labels, then Playwright selects that label.

evidence.observation: askJev is called with task, page, dropdown description, and option list; the chosen index picks the label passed to selectOption.

observed.claim: After Jev returns an action id, execution and change detection are ordinary deterministic browser code.

evidence.observation: back/scroll/fill/click run in branches; outcome is from url/title/textLength/scroll deltas or action error, not from Jev.

observed.claim: The file states a split: control flow in code, judgments in Jev.

evidence.observation: Top-of-file comment assigns judgments to Jev and control flow to code.

inferred.claim: Jev is used because matching an arbitrary natural-language task to a live, partially observed page is a semantic pick among competing controls, not a computable predicate.

evidence.observation: Inputs are language and a generated action list; the only next-act output consumed is Jev's choice, not a scored heuristic over attributes.

inferred.claim: goal_done and stuck are Jev because whether a page satisfies a task or a history is looping is graded and page-specific.

evidence.observation: Code only compares noul scores to a fixed cutoff; it does not implement goal or loop detectors on url or DOM.

inferred.claim: Dropdown option selection is the same kind of task-to-label match, so it is a nested Jev choice rather than first-option or exact string match.

evidence.observation: Options are passed as labels with the task; the program uses Jev's choice index instead of comparing strings to the task.

unknown: Why the author chose Jev versus a general tool-calling LLM agent or a scripted planner
Why the stop cutoff is 0.85 rather than another threshold
Whether a deterministic alternative was tried and failed
How often Jev's action or watchers are wrong on real sites
Caller-side task wording quality, which the repo does not constrain

deterministic_alternative.what_rules_would_need: Per-task success detectors on url/title/text; loop detectors on history; and a ranking from goal words to live controls, plus a label matcher for every select. That implies site-specific selectors and goal predicates for unbounded pages and tasks.
deterministic_alternative.adequacy: Fragile to impossible. Tasks and DOMs are open-ended, labels are short and aliased, and done/stuck are readings of page plus history. Exact rules would overfit sites and miss paraphrased goals.
